A wristband identifies an active shopping session. An identity read establishes cart context; it does not by itself prove who picked up an item.
A load-cell change and RFID observations form a candidate shelf event. Calibration, product weight variation and simultaneous actions still need controlled testing.
A detected event must be matched to one valid shopping session before a cart changes. Ambiguous candidates stay on hold for review.
A return references an earlier accepted pickup. The inverse event changes quantity while preserving both actions in the history.
Accepted events determine quantities and subtotal. Held events stay separate so uncertainty cannot silently become a charge.
The final accepted cart becomes an invoice summary. Payment processing and a commercial deployment are separate from this prototype.
